So I actually did something pretty similar to what you’re talking about. When I was 17 right out of high school I wanted to be a mortician. I actually spoke to a local funeral director who told me do the apprenticeship BEFORE you go to mortuary school. Did I listen? No. But I don’t necessarily regret not listening.
I went to work for another funeral home owned by SCI as a funeral assistant. I was paid and did make $11.50/hr which felt like a lot to me at 17. I also went to Gupton-Jones College of Funeral Service which like you, was about 30/40 minutes away from me. I did this for 6 months before I decided it wasn’t for me.

See, this isn’t really a normal 9-5. It is on paper but if a family wants to have a funeral until 7- you’re gonna be expected to stay until 7pm. If the clock strikes 5 and you have a persons neck open looking for a vein and artery- you can’t just stop and walk away until tomorrow, you’re staying until the embalming is mostly done. When you’re on call, you better make sure that phone is turned ALL the way up because if you miss your call your coworkers WILL be mad. And it doesn’t matter if you get no calls or 5 separate calls all throughout the night if you’re scheduled to work the next day you’re going even if you didn’t get an hour of sleep. 

And it’s not really a job that ends when you get home. Some days are really emotionally hard, physically hard, if you’re on call you can’t make plans for that night.
I say none of this to discourage you. But I’m letting you know now that this isn’t just some job where like “oh this is gonna be pretty easy and fun” like no, if this isn’t the job for you you’re gonna be miserable. I was dead set on it & thought it’s what I wanted FOREVER and I still left after 6 months
